title: One titration, one exact balance, four useful approximations
promptMarkdown: A hypothetical ideal acid HA has $K_a=2.00\times10^{-5}$ at $25^\circ\mathrm C$. Start with $30.0\,\mathrm{mL}$ of $0.0800\,\mathrm M$ acid and consider adding $0.120\,\mathrm M$ sodium hydroxide. Volumes add. (1) Find the equivalence volume. (2) For an arbitrary added volume $V$, express the total acid concentration $C_T$ and sodium concentration $C_N$, then derive a single equation for $h$ using $[A^-]=C_TK_a/(K_a+h)$ and charge balance. (3) Calculate justified approximate pH values at $V=0$, $10.0$, $20.0$ and $25.0\,\mathrm{mL}$. (4) Explain why the four points require different approximations, why the equivalence pH is not seven, and what changes if the temperature changes. (5) Propose a numerical residual check that would detect an inaccurate approximation near equivalence without treating agreement with one formula as proof.
hintLadder: The total acid amount is conserved even though its protonation changes.
The strong base contributes a sodium spectator ion, whether hydroxide remains or has reacted.
Use stoichiometry to identify each region, then test its approximation in the single balance equation.

criteria.criterion: Derives total-volume concentrations and a valid complete charge-balance equation.
